record.original_question: Let f1 , ..., fk be bounded holomorphic functions on Omega. SupP pose |fi | > c > 0. The Corona problem is whether there exist bounded P holomorphic funcions g1 , ..., gk on Omega such that fi gi ≡ 1. Can the Corona problem be solved if Omega is the unit ball or the unit polydisc?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2.1 Let f1 , ..., fk be bounded holomorphic functions on Ω. SupP pose |fi | > c > 0. The Corona problem is whether there exist bounded P holomorphic funcions g1 , ..., gk on Ω such that fi gi ≡ 1. Can the Corona problem be solved if Ω is the unit ball or the unit polydisc? 5.3 Hyper-holomorphic functions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega$ denote either the open unit ball $\mathbb{B}^n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z| < 1\}$ or the open unit polydisc $\mathbb{D}^n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z_j| < 1 \text{ for all } j\}$, with $n \geq 2$. Let $H^\infty(\Omega)$ denote the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\Omega$ with the supremum norm.

Suppose $f_1, \dots, f_k \in H^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfy the joint lower bound
$$\max_{1 \le i \le k} |f_i(z)| \ge c > 0 \quad \text{for every } z \in \Omega,$$
for some constant $c > 0$.

Determine whether there must exist functions $g_1, \dots, g_k \in H^\infty(\Omega)$ such that
$$\sum_{i=1}^{k} f_i(z)\, g_i(z) = 1 \quad \text{for every } z \in \Omega.$$

Equivalently, decide whether the maximal ideal space of $H^\infty(\Omega)$ has the evaluations at points of $\Omega$ as a dense subset (the "corona problem") when $\Omega$ is the unit ball $\mathbb{B}^n$ or the polydisc $\mathbb{D}^n$ with $n \ge 2$.
artifact.category_tag: Corona problem in several complex variables
artifact.status_search_result: The classical corona problem for $H^\infty$ of the unit ball $\mathbb{B}^n$ and the polydisc $\mathbb{D}^n$ in dimension $n \ge 2$ remains open. While related results have been established (e.g., Toeplitz/baby corona theorems, $H^p$ corona for $p < \infty$, and corona theorems on specific subdomains), the $p=\infty$ corona problem in several variables is still unresolved as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: The Corona Problem, Carleson Measures, and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: There are very simple domains such as the unit ball or the polydisc for which the Corona problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The corona problem on the ball and polydisc remains open.

status_evidence.title: Connections of the Corona Problem with Operator Theory and Complex Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: The Corona theorem in the unit ball would require a result with p = +infty and this question is still open for n >= 2.
status_evidence.claim: H^infty corona problem in the ball is open for n >= 2.
